newsitem.title: USA: Major stock weekend movements - Oct 7.
newsitem.headline: Major stock weekend movements - Oct 7.

text.p: WASHINGTON - The U.S. unemployment rate edged up to 5.2 percent last month from 5.1 percent as jobs vanished for the first time in eight months, the government said Friday, reflecting an end-of-summer economic cool-down. In the government's first assessment of the economy's health in September, the Labour Department said the number of non-farm jobs unexpectedly shrank by 40,000 during the month, after payrolls grew by 241,000 in August. Economists, on average, had expected an increase of 166,000 jobs last month.

LONDON - The stock market shot to record highs after surprisingly weak U.S. employment data sent bonds and Wall Street soaring. The FTSE 100 index set a new all-time high of 4,025.1 points some 10 minutes before the close before ending at a record finish of 4,024.8, up 24.8 points on the day and 60.7 from Friday a week ago.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended thin bourse trade slightly higher at another record high as a firm dollar underpinned the market. The 30-share DAX index closed 6.78 points higher at 2,683.28 and up 37.18 from last week. In post-bourse trade, it stood at 2,704.25.

PARIS - French shares ran up solid gains, emboldened by bonds, which welcomed weak U.S. September employment figures. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed 16.60 points or 0.78 percent ahead at 2,152.69, up 73.23 from seven days ago.

ZURICH - Swiss blue-chip shares were propelled higher by weaker-than-expected U.S. jobs figures, which eased fears that U.S. interest rates might rise soon. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) firmed 16.69 points or 0.69 percent to 2,431.91, rising 63.49 from last week.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks tumbled as market participants backed off to the sidelines ahead of the weekend and to wait for U.S. payrolls data. The benchmark Nikkei 225 index slid 183.47 points or 0.86 percent to close at 21,148.03 but showed a rise of 35.79 on the week.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's blue chips snapped a seven-session winning streak to end sharply lower as the market took a rest from its recent ascent. The Hang Seng index closed 109.05 points lower at 11,905.51 but recorded a gain of 313.15 from a week ago.

SYDNEY - Australian shares closed mixed on profit-taking, waning late in the session, but investors were still cautious ahead of the release of U.S. payrolls data. The benchmark all ordinaries index ended 0.6 points up at 2,315.5 for a gain of 74.7 since last Friday.

JOHANNESBURG - A sturdy bullion price supported South African gold shares and dealers said that if bullion held its head up, golds could firm further next week. The overall index ended up 6.1 points at 7,020.6, rising 85.3 from seven days ago. Industrials were off 3.7 points to 8,222.4 but up 31.6 from last Friday.
